note: FROZEN. These are the four tools the Needle feasibility spike used, kept verbatim so the device findings of 2026-09-22 remain reproducible against the corpus that records them. Nothing is trained against this schema: control_light and open_app do not exist in Vesta's tool registry, and set_timer here takes duration_seconds where production takes minutes. v2 (tools/tool-schema-v2.json) is derived from the production registry and is the surface that is trained and released. This file and data/historical/ exist so a spike result can still be read in the terms it was produced in — not as a training target.

duration_seconds.description: How long the timer should run, in seconds.
duration_seconds.note: The spike's finding 1: 'Set a timer for 20 minutes.' came back as 20, not 1200. Unit normalization is Vesta's responsibility at dispatch, and the router is still evaluated on getting it right — a router that emits the wrong unit forces the deterministic layer to guess which unit it meant.

tools.name: set_alarm
tools.description: Set an alarm at a clock time.

time.note: The DATE is not a parameter. Vesta's deterministic scheduling layer resolves days, and its grounding guard refuses a temporal value the user never said.

tools.name: control_light
tools.description: Turn a light on or off in a named room.

room.description: The room, in the user's own words. Not normalized here.

app_name.description: The application as the user named it. Resolving it to a package is Vesta's job.

outcomes.tool: An executable action with every required argument present AND grounded in the user's own words.
outcomes.incomplete: The request names a tool but a required argument has no evidence. NOT an action. Vesta asks.
outcomes.cancel: The user abandoned or cancelled a pending action.
outcomes.chat: No action. The request belongs to the conversational model.
